course.power.title: Computer Vision Notes
group.basics.title: Basic levels
level.projection.after: The image is f·H/Z tall: only the ratio of f to Z counts, and the brightness only the hole and f. Moving the plate changes Z and f together.
With the plate where it is, where must the screen go for a 40 mm image?
The screen back where it was; this time move only the plate, for a 40 mm image again.
Both move now: a 40 mm image, and the screen no darker than at the start.
level.projection.tasks.projection.brief: The image in the camera obscura is 20 mm tall. Each step makes it 40 mm using only the knobs the step opens. Work out where first, then check.
level.projection.title: Pinhole projection and depth ambiguity
level.separable.after: Only a kernel that is a column times a row runs as a pass across then a pass down; the Laplacian is no product but the sum of two second differences, across and down.
level.separable.tasks.separable.brief: The Laplacian 0 1 0 / 1 −4 1 / 0 1 0 is no column times a row. Can 1D three-point kernels alone compute it? Make the output match it.
level.separable.title: Separable filters and their cost
level.sinusoid.after: The average moves the whole wave up or down, the amplitude sets how high it swings, the frequency how many cycles fit in the row, and the phase only slides it sideways; half a cycle of phase looks like the swing turned over.
level.sinusoid.tasks.sinusoid.bench.stag: The target sits a little to the left of your wave.
The target is light where your wave is dark.
level.sinusoid.tasks.sinusoid.brief: Each step’s target differs from your wave in one number. Judge which one and by how much, turn only that one, then check.
level.sinusoid.title: Frequency, amplitude and phase
